title: Organisation and Management
author: 3iGR44tcGMnRnhEYm
chapter_outcomes: Explain why people work and what motivation means with its importance, analyse the benefits of a well-motivated workforce (labour productivity, reduced absenteeism and labour turnover), and evaluate human needs (Maslow) and key motivational theories (Taylor and Herzberg).

Describe financial (e.g wages, bonus) and non-financial (e.g job enrichment, training) methods of motivation and recommend and justify the most appropriate method(s) of motivation in given circumstances.

Draw, interpret and explain simple organisational charts, including levels of hierarchy, span of control, chain of command, and the roles, responsibilities and relationships of employees within an organisation and inter relationships between them
Explain the role and functions of management, including planning, organising, coordinating, commanding and controlling, and assess the importance of delegation, trust and control.
Describe the main leadership styles (autocratic, democratic and laissez-faire) and recommend and justify an appropriate leadership style in given circumstances.
Understand what a trade union is and assess the effects of employees being members of trade unions.

Understand recruitment and selection methods, distinguish between internal and external recruitment, describe the main stages of recruitment and selection, and recommend and justify who to employ, including the benefits and limitations of part-time and full-time employees.
Understand the importance of training to businesses and employees and evaluate the benefits and limitations of induction, on-the-job and off-the-job training.

Explain the difference between dismissal and redundancy with examples, analyse situations where workforce reduction is necessary, and recommend and justify which employees should be made redundant in given circumstances.
Explain legal controls over employment issues, including contracts, unfair dismissal, discrimination, health and safety, and minimum wage, and assess their impact on employers and employees.

Explain the importance of effective communication, evaluate the benefits and limitations of different communication methods (including IT-based methods), and recommend and justify appropriate communication methods in given circumstances.
Explain how communication barriers arise, the problems caused by ineffective communication, and how communication barriers can be reduced or removed.
